page: Amazon Web Services p6-b200.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro system architecture, tailored for distributed high-performance computing and large-scale artificial intelligence workloads. It integrates 192 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.4 GHz across 96 physical Intel cores with simultaneous multithreading. System memory capacity totals 2048 GB, yielding approximately 10.67 GB of memory per core to support memory-heavy host operations, complex pre-processing routines, and extensive data staging.

GPU acceleration is anchored by eight NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs supplying a combined 1432 GB of high-bandwidth GPU memory. For fast local access to training datasets, checkpoints, and intermediate scratch data, the instance includes 30400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1600 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node communication essential for scaling synchronized distributed pipelines across multiple instances.

From a resource and architectural standpoint, the p6-b200.48xlarge represents an extreme density tier where massive GPU VRAM and ultra-high networking bandwidth dominate the footprint. The fixed inclusion of 30.4 TB of local NVMe storage and dedicated core allocation targets environments where data ingestion bottlenecks must be minimized. The instance is suited for foundational large language model training, distributed multi-GPU deep learning, large-scale generative AI inference, and computationally intensive scientific simulations requiring extensive parallel compute.
